## Natural history notes

A medium-sized carrion beetle characterized by its flattened dark body, broad wing covers, and reddish-orange markings or margins that give it a red-lined appearance. In Florida, it is found in forests, hammocks, pine flatwoods, fields, roadsides, parks, and other habitats where carrion or decaying organic material is available. Adults and larvae feed on carrion and other decomposing animal matter, helping recycle nutrients, and adults may also prey on fly larvae and other small insects associated with carcasses.
